Rashi on Menachot 22a:1:1.hebrew: כי זכי להו רחמנא - לשכה למלוח קרבנם משל הקדש, לישראל הוא דזכי להו, משום דאית להו לשכה, כלומר: שהם נתנו השקלים בלשכה שמהן נקנה המלח; אבל כהנים שאין חייבין לשקול - לא. להכי איצטריך תנאה:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:1:1.english: When the Merciful One granted them - [The supplies of the] chamber to salt their offerings from consecrated property, it was to Israelites that He granted [this], because they have [a share in the] chamber, that is to say, they gave the shekels to the chamber from which the salt is purchased; but priests, who are not obligated to contribute the shekel — [He did] not [grant it to them]. For this [reason], the stipulation [of the court] was necessary.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:3:1.english: New - According to Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua, we require new [wood].

Rashi on Menachot 22a:4:1.english: Here too, with new ones - That Araunah had not yet used them.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:1.english: A goat - An iron goat is placed upon it to weigh it down.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:2.english: A goat of a kurkesa - A kurkesa is a large board full of pegs.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:3.hebrew: דדיישי דישא - שנותנין אותו על התבואה, וקושרין בו שוורים ומושכין אותו, ונידושת התבואה:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:3.english: That they thresh the grain - That they place it upon the grain, tie oxen to it, and pull it, and the grain is threshed.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:4.hebrew: מאי קרא - מוריגים לצורך דישה, דכתיב מורג וכתיב תדוש:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:4.english: What is the verse - [Showing that] morigim are for the purpose of threshing? As it is written: "morag," and it is written: "you shall thresh."

Rashi on Menachot 22a:5:5.english: Tightly fastened - Well and firmly secured.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:6:1.english: With the meal offering of priests, it is fit - For all of it is wholly burned, just like it.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:1.hebrew: ר' יהודה אומר אם נתערב הקומץ במנחת נסכים ומנחת כהן משיח פסולה - לפי שהקומץ דמנחת נדבת ישראל בלילתו עבה, לוג לעשרון:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: If the handful was intermingled with the meal offering of libations and the meal offering of the anointed priest, it is unfit - Because [with regard to] the handful of the voluntary meal offering of an Israelite, its mixture is thick: one log [of oil] per tenth of an ephah [issaron].

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:2.hebrew: ומנחת כהן משיח ומנחת נסכים בלילתן רכה, שלשה לוגין לעשרון, דכתיב במנחת נסכים: בלול ברביעית ההין שמן, ויליף חביתין מינה שלשה לוגין לעשרון בפ' התכלת (לקמן מנחות נא.):
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:2.english: And [with regard to] the meal offering of the anointed priest and the meal offering of libations, their mixture is loose: three log [of oil] per tenth of an ephah [issaron], as it is written concerning the meal offering of libations: "Mixed with a fourth of a hin of oil," and [the Gemara] derives [the requirement of the] chavitin [the meal offering of the anointed priest] from it: three log per tenth of an ephah, in chapter HaTekhelet (below, Menachot 51a).

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:3.hebrew: והן בולעות זו מזו - הקומץ בולע ממנחת נסכים, והוה ליה ריבה שמנה, ומנחת נסכים נמי פסולה, דהוה ליה חיסר שמנה. והאי דקתני פסולה ולא קתני פסולות, משום דכולה מתניתין בלישנא דחדא מנחה איירי. ורישא נמי הכי תנא: נתערב קומצה בקומץ חבירתה כשרה, והוה ליה למיתני כשרות:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:3.english: And they absorb from each other - The handful absorbs [oil] from the meal offering of libations, and [thus] it has an excess of oil; and the meal offering of libations is also unfit, because it has a deficiency of oil. And as for that which [the mishna] teaches "it is unfit" [in the singular] and does not teach "they are unfit" [in the plural], [this is] because the entire mishna speaks in the phrasing of a single meal offering. And the first clause [of the mishna] also taught like this: "If its handful was mixed with the handful of another, it is fit" — whereas it should have taught: "they are fit."

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:4.hebrew: אם יכול לקמוץ מזו בפני עצמה - שנפלה זו בצד זו, ונשאר מזו כדי קומץ שלא נתערב, כשרות; ואם לאו, פסולות, דאמר בתורת כהנים: מסלתה ולא מסלת חבירתה:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:4.english: If one can remove a handful from this one by itself - [Such as] where one fell beside the other, and there remained from this [one] enough for a handful that did not become mixed, they are fit; and if not, they are unfit, as it says in Torat Kohanim: "From its fine flour" — and not from the fine flour of another [meal offering].

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:5.hebrew: לא יקטיר - אפי' כל המעורבת, דאין הקטרה מצוה אלא בקומץ, ומקמץ נמי לא מצי קמיץ שני קומצים, דדלמא בכל קומץ וקומץ יש מזה שנתערב, וליכא קומץ שלם מחמת מנחה:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:5.english: He may not burn - Even the entire mixture, for burning is not a mitzvah except with a handful; and as for taking a handful, he also cannot take two handfuls, since perhaps in each and every handful there is [some] of that which was intermingled, and there is no complete handful from [a single] meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:6.hebrew: ואם הקטיר - כל המעורבת, היא לא עלתה לבעלים, דהא לא נקמצה, ואין מנחת נדבה נתרת בלא קמיצה:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:6.english: And if he burned - [Even if he burned] the entire mixture, it [the un-scooped offering] did not satisfy the owner's obligation, as a handful was not scooped from it, and a voluntary meal offering is not permitted without scooping [a handful].

Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:7.hebrew: נתערב קומצה בשיריה - לא יקטיר את כולה, משום דשירים אסורין להקטיר, דכתיב: לא תקטירו ממנו אשה לה' (ויקרא ב׳:י״א) — כל שממנו לאשים, הרי הוא בבל תקטירו:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:7:7.english: Its handful was intermingled with its remainder - He should not burn the entirety of it, because remainders are forbidden to be burned [on the altar], as it is written: "You shall not burn of it an offering made by fire to the Lord" (Leviticus 2:11) — anything from which [part] is [offered] to the fires is subject to [the prohibition of] "You shall not burn."

Rashi on Menachot 22a:8:3.english: [If] it was mixed with wine - Which is red.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:8:4.hebrew: רואין אותו כאילו הוא מים - ואם היה מים והיה מראית הדם ניכר ביניהם, כשר:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:8:4.english: One views it as though it were water - And if it were water and the appearance of the blood would be discernible among them, it is fit.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:8:5.english: With the blood of a domesticated animal - Of non-sacred [animals].

Rashi on Menachot 22a:8:7.english: Blood does not nullify blood - And [it is] fit.

Rashi on Menachot 22a:9:1.hebrew: הדבר ידוע כו' - אפילו הכי קרי ליה אכתי נמי דם שעיר, ואף על פי שנתערב בו דם הפר, כדאמרינן במסכת יומא (דף נג:): עירה דם הפר לתוך דם השעיר:
Rashi on Menachot 22a:9:1.english: It is a known matter, etc. - Even so, [the verse] still calls it "the blood of the goat" as well, even though the blood of the bull was mixed into it, as we say in Tractate Yoma (page 53b): "He poured the blood of the bull into the blood of the goat."

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:2:1.hebrew: ועצים דפשיטא ליה לתנא משל צבור מנלן - וא"ת: ולילף ממלח כדלעיל, דאין להשיב מלבונה? ושמא יש צד אחד:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:2:1.english: And wood, concerning which it is obvious to the Tanna [that it comes] from communal [supplies], from where do we [derive this]? - And if you say: Let [the Tanna] derive [wood] from salt, as above, for one cannot refute [this derivation] from frankincense? And perhaps there is one distinguishing aspect [that refutes it].

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:1.hebrew: שזו בלילתה עבה - מנחת נדבה, ולוג לעשרון, כדדרשי' בפ' שתי מדות (לקמן מנחות פט.), כדכתיב במצורע עני: "ועשרון סלת בלול בשמן למנחה ולוג שמן", דמייתא ליה "למנחה ולוג שמן" למתנדב מנחה, לא יפחות מדבר הטעון לוג, ומאי ניהו? עשרון. ומנחת הנסכים וכהן משיח שלשה לוגין לעשרון, כדמפרש בקונט':
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:1.english: For this one, its mixture is thick - [This refers to] a voluntary meal offering, and [there is] a log [of oil] per tenth [of an ephah], as we derive in the chapter [entitled] "Shtei Middot" (below, Menachot 89a), as it is written regarding a poor leper: "And a tenth-part of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil" (Leviticus 14:21), where it adduces [the phrase] "for a meal offering, and a log of oil" [to teach regarding] one who volunteers a meal offering, that he may not [bring] less than an item that requires a log — and what is that? A tenth [of an ephah]. And the meal offering of libations and [that of the] anointed priest [require] three logs per tenth [of an ephah], as is explained in the Kuntres [Rashi].

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:2.hebrew: שזו בלילתה עבה וזו בלילתה רכה והן בולעות זו מזו - אע"ג דקתני פסולה, דמשמע האחת, נראה דשתיהן פסולות, העבה והרכה, מדקתני והן בולעות זו מזו. ומיהו בבליעה חדא מיפסלי תרווייהו: דכי בלע קומץ ממנחת נסכים, מיפסיל קומץ דהוה ליה ריבה שמנה, ומיפסלא מנחת נסכים דהוה ליה חיסר שמנה. והא דקתני פסולה ולא קתני פסולות, משום דכולה מתניתין בלישנא דחדא מנחה איירי; ורישא נמי הכי תנן: נתערב קומצה בקומץ של חבירתה כשרה, והוה ליה למיתני כשרות. וכששתיהן בלילתן עבה או רכה, אף על פי שבולעות זו מזו, לא חשיב לא ריבה שמנה ולא חיסר שמנה, ולא מפסלא:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:2.english: Because this one's mixture is thick and that one's mixture is loose, and they absorb from each other - Even though [the Mishnah] teaches "[it is] disqualified" (pesulah), which implies [only] one [of them], it appears that both of them are disqualified, [both] the thick and the loose, since it teaches: "and they absorb from each other." And yet, through a single absorption both of them become disqualified: for when the handful absorbs [oil] from the meal offering of libations, the handful is disqualified, as it has [a status of] "increased its oil" (ribah shamnah), and the meal offering of libations is disqualified, as it has [a status of] "decreased its oil" (chisar shamnah). And that which it teaches "[it is] disqualified" and does not teach "[they are] disqualified" (pesulot) is because the entire Mishnah speaks in the phrasing of a single meal offering. And in the first clause (reisha) we also learned likewise: "If its handful was intermingled with the handful of its fellow, it is valid" (kesherah), whereas it should have taught: "[they are] valid" (kesherot). And when both of their mixtures are thick, or [both are] loose, even though they absorb from each other, it is considered neither "increased its oil" nor "decreased its oil", and neither is disqualified.

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:3.hebrew: והן בולעות זו מזו - פי' בקונטרס: הקומץ בולע מן מנחת נסכים, והוה ליה ריבה שמנה. ובגמ', גבי הא דפריך לרב חסדא דאמר בתר מבטל אזלינן ממתניתין דשתי מנחות שלא נקמצו, דאם יכול לקמוץ מזו בפני עצמה ומזו בפני עצמה כשרה, והא כיון דקמיץ ליה מחדא אידך הוה ליה שיריים, ולא מבטל ליה שיריים לטיבלא — ופי' בקונטרס שטיבלא דלא מבטל להו לשיריים דניהוו כריבה סולתה, לא מצי למיפרך לרבי חנינא דנימא מהכא דבתר מבטל אזלינן: דאי בתר בטל אזלינן, שיריים מי הוי טיבלא? דאי נמי בתר בטל אזלינן וטיבלא מבטל לשיריים, לא הוי ריבה סולתה, דבטילי וכמאן דליתיה דמי, ולא מייתר ליה. ופירוש זה סותר מה שפירש במשנה, דמהאי טעמא לא יחשוב כמו ריבה שמנה. ואין לפרש דמה דמיפסלן הכא לאו משום ריבה שמנה אלא משום חיסר שמנה; דאדרבה, לפי מה שמפרש בגמ' גבי חרב שנתערב בבלול, לא מיפסלן אלא משום ריבה שמנה:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:3.english: And they absorb from each other - Rashi explained: The handful absorbs from the meal offering of libations, and [thus] it becomes [an offering that has] excess oil. And in the Gemara, regarding that which [the Gemara] objects to Rav Chisda, who said, "We follow the [potentially] nullifying substance," from the mishna of two meal offerings from which handfuls had not been removed—[which teaches] that if one can remove a handful from this one by itself and from that one by itself, it is fit, [and the Gemara objects:] yet once he removed a handful from one, the rest of it becomes remainder, so why does the remainder not nullify the un-taken offering?—and Rashi explained that [as for why] the un-taken offering does not nullify the remainder so that they would become like [an offering with] excess flour, [the Gemara] could not object to Rabbi Chanina [so as] to say from here that we follow the nullifying substance: For if we follow the nullified substance, can remainder ever become an un-taken offering? And furthermore, even if we follow the nullified substance and the un-taken offering nullifies the remainder, it would not be [considered] excess flour, as they are nullified and are considered as though non-existent, and [thus] it does not create an excess. And this explanation contradicts what he explained in the mishna, as for this [same] reason it should not be considered like excess oil! And one cannot explain that the reason they are invalidated here is not because of excess oil, but rather because of deficient oil; for on the contrary, according to what he explains in the Gemara regarding a dry [meal offering] that was intermingled with an oiled [meal offering], they are invalidated only because of excess oil.

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:4.hebrew: והן בולעות זו מזו - מין בשאינו מינו חשיב ליה בגמרא, משום דאמרי' סלק את מינו כמי שאינו, ושאינו מינו רבה עליו ומבטלו, שהסולת של קומץ רבה על השמן של מנחת נסכים ומבטלו. ותימה, דמהאי טעמא נמי ליפסול לרבי יהודה נתערב קומצה בקומץ חבירתה! וזה הוא תימה לומר: משום דבלילתן שוות אין זו בולעת מזו. ועוד, נתערב קומצה בשיריה, דקתני סיפא דאם הקטיר עלתה לבעלים, ופריך מינה בגמרא: דליבטלו שיריים לקומץ, ומשני ר' זירא: נאמרה הקטרה בקומץ כו' — למה לן האי שינויא? הא אמרינן דבלילתן שוות ואין בולעות זו מזו, ומאי אין קומץ מבטל קומץ שייך כאן? ועוד תימה, דבגזירה שוה דר' זירא אליבא דרבי יהודה נמי מסקי לה, ומשמע דאין הקומץ מבטל חבירו, אפי' קומץ דמנחת חוטא וקומץ דמנחת נדבה, אף על פי שזה חרב וזה בלול. ומה שכתוב בספרים בגמ' גבי חרב שנתערב עם בלול: "מאי לאו קומץ דמנחת חוטא דאיערב בקומץ דמנחת נדבה" — לא גרסינן הכי, אלא כספרים דגרסי: "דאיערב במנחת נסכים"; אבל שום קומץ אין מבטל חבירו, אפי' לרבי יהודה, דאי משכחת חד קומץ דמבטל, לא תתקיים גזירה שוה. והשתא, מנלן לרבי יהודה דלא יבטלו זה את זה קומץ דמנחת חוטא וקומץ דמנחת נדבה? הא בלעי מהדדי! ועוד תימה: למאי דמסקינן מגזירה שוה דר' זירא אליבא דר' יהודה, א"כ מנחת נסכים וקומץ נמי לא ליבטלו זה את זה. ומיהו הא לאו פירכא היא, דדוקא בקומץ ושיריים איכא גזירה שוה דהקטרה הקטרה, אבל מנחת נסכים כולה כליל, ואין כאן קומץ ושיריים:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:7:4.english: And they absorb from each other - The Gemara considers it [a mixture of] a substance with a different substance because we say: Disregard its own substance as though it were not [there], and that which is of a different substance is greater than it and nullifies it — as the fine flour of the handful is greater [in volume] than the oil of the meal offering of libations and nullifies it. And it is difficult: for based on this reason, let [a case where] its handful was mixed with the handful of another [meal offering] also be disqualified according to Rabbi Yehuda! And it is astonishing to say: [namely,] that because their mixtures are equal [in consistency], neither absorbs from the other. Furthermore, [in the case where] its handful was mixed with its remainders, which the latter clause [of the mishna] teaches that if he burned [it], it satisfies the obligation of the owner, and the Gemara raises an objection from it: let the remainders nullify the handful! And Rabbi Zeira answers: "Burning is stated regarding a handful, etc." — why do we need this resolution? Behold, we say that because their mixtures are equal, they do not absorb from each other! And what does [the principle that] "a handful does not nullify a handful" have to do here? And furthermore, it is difficult: for according to the verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) of Rabbi Zeira, they conclude [the discussion] even according to Rabbi Yehuda; and this implies that a handful does not nullify another [handful], even the handful of a sinner's meal offering and the handful of a voluntary meal offering, even though this one is dry and that one is mixed [with oil]. And as for that which is written in the books in the Gemara regarding "a dry [meal offering] that was mixed with an oiled [meal offering]: is it not the handful of a sinner's meal offering that was mixed with the handful of a voluntary meal offering?": we do not have this reading; rather, [our reading is] like the books that read: "that was mixed with a meal offering of libations." For no handful nullifies another [handful], even according to Rabbi Yehuda; because if you were to find even a single handful that nullifies [another], the verbal analogy could not stand! And now: from where do we know according to Rabbi Yehuda that they do not nullify one another — the handful of a sinner's meal offering and the handful of a voluntary meal offering? Behold, they absorb from each other! And furthermore, it is difficult: according to that which we conclude from the verbal analogy of Rabbi Zeira according to Rabbi Yehuda, if so, a meal offering of libations and a handful should also not nullify one another! However, this is no refutation, for only regarding a handful and remainders is there a verbal analogy of "burning" [and] "burning" (haktarah haktarah); but a meal offering of libations is completely burned (kalil), and there is no handful and remainders here.

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:8:1.hebrew: אם יש בו מראית דם כשר - לא באדמומית מעט מתכשר, אלא מראית דם גמור קאמר, למעוטי היכא דדיהה מראיתו. דהא דדם הפר מרובה על דמו של שעיר, משמע דאי לאו מטעם עולין או משום מין במינו, היה בטל, אע"פ שאם היה דמו של פר מים, היה בו מראית דם שעיר קצת:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:8:1.english: If it has the appearance of blood, it is fit - It is not rendered fit by [merely] a slight redness; rather, [the Tanna] means the appearance of complete blood, to exclude [a case] where its appearance has faded. For [the fact] that the blood of the bull is more than the blood of the goat implies that were it not for the reason of [items that] ascend [the altar] (olin) or because of like [substance] with like [substance] (min be-mino), it would be nullified — even though if the blood of the bull were water, there would [still] be a slight appearance of the goat's blood in it.

Tosafot on Menachot 22a:9:1.hebrew: הדבר ידוע שדמו של פר מרובה על דמו של שעיר - פי', והיה לו לדמו של שעיר להיות בטל. תימה, דאיפכא הוה ליה למידק, דאמרינן ביומא (דף נג:) שעירב דם הפר בדם השעיר. וההיא דדם שנתערב במים, אמרי' בפ' התערובות (זבחים עח:) ובפרק כיסוי הדם (חולין פז:): לא שנו אלא שנפלו מים לתוך דם, אבל דם לתוך מים - ראשון ראשון בטל; והילכך, האי דם הפר היה לו להבטל ראשון ראשון בדם השעיר. ואפי' מאן דלית ליה ראשון ראשון בטל בפ' בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (דף עג.), הכא מודה, משום דהוה ליה נראה ונדחה. וי"ל, דלא אמרינן ראשון ראשון בטל כשמערה בשפע הרבה ביחד, כמו שמחלק בפרק בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (שם) בין חבית דנפיש עמודיה לצרצור קטן דלא נפיש עמודיה; ואפילו מאן דאית ליה ראשון ראשון בטל בחבית, ביותר מפי חבית היה מודה דלא בטל:
Tosafot on Menachot 22a:9:1.english: It is a known matter that the blood of the bull is more than the blood of the goat - Meaning, [ordinarily] the blood of the goat should have been nullified [by the larger volume of the bull's blood]. [This is] puzzling, for [the Gemara] should have inferred the opposite: As we say in Yoma (53b) that he mixed the blood of the bull into the blood of the goat; and [regarding] that [teaching] of blood that became mixed with water, we say in the chapter [entitled] "Ha-Ta'arovot" (Zevachim 78b) and in the chapter [entitled] "Kisui Ha-Dam" (Chullin 87b): They taught [that it remains fit] only where water fell into blood, but [if] blood [fell] into water, each [portion] is nullified bit by bit (rishon rishon batel) [as it enters]. And therefore, this blood of the bull should have been nullified bit by bit in the blood of the goat! And even the one who does not maintain [the principle of] "nullified bit by bit" (rishon rishon batel) in the last chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (73a), here he would concede, because it is [a case of] having been fit and [then] rejected (nir'eh ve-nidcha) [which cannot become fit again]. And one can say that we do not say "nullified bit by bit" when one pours in great abundance all at once, as [the Gemara] distinguishes in the last chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (ibid.) between a barrel whose stream is thick and a small pitcher whose stream is not thick; and even the one who maintains [that it is] nullified bit by bit in [the case of] a barrel would concede that [when poured with a flow] greater than the mouth of a barrel, it is not nullified.
